title_or_subject: Unnumbered executive order reserving public lands in San Juan County, Washington Territory, for lighthouse purposes (several light-station sites: Lime Kiln, and portions of Jones Island and Matia Island)
president: Ulysses S. Grant (by date; no source fetched names him)

sources.what: Federal Register 28 Sep 2010 (BLM notice, Lime Kiln Light Station, San Juan County WA)
sources.quote: The reservation of public land for the Lime Kiln Light Station created by an Executive Order dated July 15, 1875

sources.what: APP: EO 7595 (Matia Island, signed 30 Mar 1937) revokes the 1875 order for that land
sources.quote: The Executive order of July 15, 1875, reserving certain public lands for lighthouse purposes, is hereby revoked

sources.what: Washington State Parks history of Jones Island
sources.quote: Portions of Jones Island were reserved for lighthouse purposes in 1875, but no lighthouse was ever built.

queries_tried: Jones Island lighthouse reservation executive order July 15, 1875 San Juan County Washington
"July 15, 1875" executive order lighthouse reserve Washington Territory islands Matia Jones Patos Sucia
notes: Citing orders (FDR, Mar-Apr 1937) establish the Jones Island and Matia Island migratory bird refuges (APP/State Parks name EO 7594 as Jones Island, EO 7595 as Matia Island) and each revoke the 1875 order for that land. The 1875 order text itself was not found; it appears to be one unnumbered order covering several San Juan Islands light sites. Worth checking the NJ unnumbered index entry for 15 Jul 1875 and General Land Office 1875/76 report.

sources.what: Wikisource mirror of EO 1011: Notes 'See related'
sources.quote: Executive Order of March 17, 1878

queries_tried: Fort Keogh military reservation Montana executive order March 17 1878 OR March 14 1878 Hayes
presidency.ucsb.edu Hayes executive order 1878 Fort Keogh
notes: The order text of EO 1011 says March 14, 1878; the Wikisource Notes link says March 17, 1878. The 1878 order itself was not found.
